1	# Spec: Model Evaluator and Typed Entry — Production API (Item 10)
2	
3	**Status:** Draft
4	**Owner:** Reid W
5	**Created:** 2026-07-12
6	**Complexity:** HIGH
7	**Branch:** constraint-exec-epic
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Problem
12	
13	The constraint-execution architecture is proven end to end but its runtime seam still lives
14	in throwaway spike code. Two spikes established the shape:
15	
16	- **S5** proved TEAx can prepare a constraint-free graph once, then evaluate ~100 typed
17	  in-memory entry mappings with a fresh execution context per case, matching file-backed
18	  outputs exactly, rejecting invalid mappings before any module runs, and writing nothing in
19	  no-persist mode (`.project/active/spike-teax-typed-entry-scalar-continuity/findings.md`).
20	- **Item 0** drove S6's study lifecycle against S4's *real* sealed package through an
21	  S5-shaped evaluator, confirming the seam holds with zero changes to the runner/store logic
22	  and naming eight schema/naming/wiring mismatches between the spike shapes and the real
23	  package (`.project/active/constraint-study-integration-spike/findings.md`).
24	
25	What does not yet exist is the production runtime the study layer (Item 11) will build on: a
26	typed in-memory entry source, a prepared-pipeline backend with the file-backed path kept for
27	audit, an immutable evidence envelope that never depends on generated classes, and one
28	normalized failure outcome that keeps "the design is infeasible" (evidence) separate from
29	"the run broke" (failure). Item 0's eight mismatches are the concrete gap list: each is a
30	schema/naming/wiring detail the production API must resolve now, before Item 11 freezes its
31	store schema against this evaluator.
32	
33	This item productionizes that seam. It is the teax half of the "Contracts and the Evaluator"
34	concept section; it does not build the study store, runner, strategies, or policy (Item 11+).
35	
36	## Success Criteria
37	
38	- [ ] **S5 invariants are kept teax tests:** mapping-vs-file case-level parity; pre-execution
39	  rejection of an invalid typed input (missing/extra/wrong-type) before any module runs;
40	  execution-context isolation across cases; and no output directory created when persistence is
41	  off.
42	- [ ] **S4-lineage packages evaluate to evidence:** evaluating a sealed generated package
43	  (Item 0's setup now; Item 9's sealed output when it lands) returns `ModelEvidence` whose
44	  constraint verdicts are projected onto generic response keys using the runtime-owned canonical
45	  vocabulary pinned in this item (`satisfied | violated | indeterminate | not_assessed`), with
46	  the full generated report attached as an opaque artifact and no generated class imported by
47	  any runtime type. This is closable in Item 10 — the vocabulary is pinned here, not deferred to
48	  Item 9.
49	- [ ] **Runtime never depends on generated classes (kept isolation test):** an import scan of
50	  the runtime evidence and entry-source modules finds no reference to any generated symbol; the
51	  modules import and construct evidence with the generated package absent from the path.
52	- [ ] **Three phases are distinguishable:** a module exception, a schema-validation rejection
53	  at entry (`entry_validation` phase), and an infeasible (`indeterminate`) verdict land in three
54	  distinguishable places — the first two as the normalized failure outcome with different
55	  phase/cause (`module_execution` vs `entry_validation`), the third as ordinary evidence, never
56	  a failure.
57	- [ ] **Non-finite input reaches the verdict, not the guard:** a well-formed candidate with a
58	  non-finite value (e.g. a NaN budget) passes entry validation and evaluates to
59	  `indeterminate` — it is never rejected as invalid input.
60	- [ ] **Both backends agree (kept parity test):** the prepared in-memory backend and the
61	  file-backed backend return the equivalent-class-equal result (defined in Known Requirements)
62	  for the same canonical inputs, with the NaN/indeterminate case in the fixture set.
63	- [ ] S5's `RootModel[float]` continuity regression test is committed — **already discharged
64	  this run** (S5 carry-forward (1)); recorded here as done, not re-planned.
65	
66	## Known Requirements
67	
68	Grading note: items forced by how the *real* generated package and TEAx validator actually
69	behave (named by Item 0) are `[HARD]`; design intents carried from the owner-ratified concept
70	and epic are `[INHERITED]` with their source cited. See `capture-fidelity.md`.
71	
72	### Typed entry source (`MappingEntrySource`)
73	
74	- **[HARD]** Typed entry is **two-level, not a flat parameter-ID→scalar map.** The real
75	  EntryPoint emits one structured channel (`toy_plant_params: ToyPlantParams`) whose *fields*
76	  are the contract parameter IDs; downstream modules field-extract
77	  (`toy_plant_params.toy_plant__Toy_Plant__plant_budget`). The entry source must express the
78	  contract at both levels — channel → model, and model field → parameter ID — not as a single
79	  flat map keyed by parameter ID. (Item 0 mismatch 1; `real_evaluator.py:evaluate`.)
80	- **[INHERITED]** **No silent coercion under any shape.** A value must never be accepted under
81	  a mismatched contract parameter ID. (concept "Contracts and the Evaluator"; S5 findings
82	  Open Questions.)
83	- **[INHERITED]** **An invalid typed input is rejected before any module executes, with a
84	  diagnostic naming expected and got types.** "Invalid" means missing, extra, or wrong-type.
85	  The rejection happens before the first module runs and names both the expected type and the
86	  type actually supplied. **Which layer performs the rejection is exactly the reserved choice**
87	  (see Open Questions): under a validate-raw source it is the entry source at field-value
88	  granularity; under an instantiated-models source the source rejects a wrong *channel-model*
89	  and the field-value check lives at the Item 11 bridge. The requirement — rejected
90	  pre-execution, expected-and-got named — holds identically under both shapes; it is the study
91	  layer's first line of defense, required behavior, not spike detail. (concept Appendix B, S5
92	  carry-forward (3).)
93	- **[HARD]** **Non-finite floats are well-formed input, not invalid input.** Entry validation
94	  rejects missing, extra, and wrong-*type* inputs before execution (at whichever layer the
95	  reserved choice places it), but must let a non-finite float (`NaN`, `inf`) through — it is a
96	  well-formed candidate that the generated Kleene predicate evaluates to `indeterminate`. Conflating non-finite with invalid would make the
97	  entire indeterminate verdict class unreachable through typed entry. (Item 0 mismatches 1–2;
98	  the real `ToyPlantParams` is a non-strict float model that accepts non-finite values.)
99	
100	### Prepared-pipeline backend and the file-backed path
101	
102	- **[INHERITED]** **Prepare once, fresh context per case.** Validate and build the pipeline
103	  topology a single time; each case evaluates in its own fresh execution context. (concept;
104	  S5.) Prepare-once measured ~64× faster than rebuild-per-case on the real package (Item 0
105	  benchmark; ~4× on S5's toy graph — the speedup scales with model-validation cost).
106	- **[INHERITED]** **The file-backed path is retained for auditable runs**, producing the same
107	  evidence plus persisted artifacts. (concept "How It Works — Evaluate One Design Point".)
108	- **[INHERITED]** **Case-level parity between the two backends is a kept test**, over an
109	  explicit equivalence class; a faster backend is admitted only on that parity. (concept;
110	  Required Invariant "auditable and fast evaluators return equivalent … results".) The
111	  equivalence class:
112	  - **Compared:** selected outputs, matched by stable ID, with **NaN-aware numeric equality** —
113	    two values are equal if they are numerically equal *or* both non-finite of the same kind
114	    (both NaN counts equal; `+inf`≡`+inf`, `-inf`≡`-inf`). Constraint verdict statuses are
115	    compared **exactly** (string equality on the canonical vocabulary).
116	  - **Excluded (enumerated):** provenance, timestamps, input digests, artifact paths, and the
117	    opaque report's on-disk encoding — the file-backed path serializes and the in-memory path
118	    does not, so byte-level report form is not a parity field.
119	  - **The NaN / indeterminate case MUST be in the parity fixture set.** It is the case the whole
120	    architecture exists to preserve, and it is exactly where a naive field compare fails: the
121	    file-backed path round-trips a NaN through JSON while the in-memory path holds a real
122	    `float('nan')`, and `NaN != NaN`. The NaN-aware rule above is what makes the two agree.
123	- **[INHERITED]** **No-persist mode writes nothing** — no output directory is created when
124	  persistence is off. (S5 findings; concept.)
125	- **[HARD]** **The validator requires ExitPoint write handlers even in no-persist mode.** A
126	  pure in-memory evaluator that never writes still must build an output router with JSON write
127	  handlers for the generated custom types, because `PipelineValidator` demands a write handler
128	  per ExitPoint output type unconditionally (validity coupled to writability). The in-memory
129	  backend must construct that router (or the design must decouple validity from writability).
130	  (Item 0 mismatch 7; `real_evaluator.py:_build_prepared`.)
131	- **[HARD]** **Evaluator protocol is `evaluate(typed_inputs) -> Evidence`** — it carries no
132	  `attempt_number`. The prepared pipeline is deterministic and stateless per case; the spike's
133	  `attempt_number` argument was unused. Retry/attempt bookkeeping belongs to the runner
134	  (Item 11), not the evaluator protocol. (Item 0 mismatch 4; `real_evaluator.py:evaluate`.)
135	
136	### `ModelEvidence`
137	
138	- **[INHERITED]** **Immutable, runtime-owned generic envelope.** `ModelEvidence` carries:
139	  response entries keyed by stable IDs (constraint verdicts project onto generic response
140	  keys), selected outputs, provenance, and the full generated report attached as an opaque
141	  model artifact. (concept "Contracts and the Evaluator".)
142	- **[INHERITED]** **Runtime types never import generated classes.** The evidence envelope and
143	  every other runtime type depend only on generic/runtime types; the generated
144	  `ConstraintReport` is held opaquely, never imported. Item 0 confirmed the generic projection
145	  is clean. (concept; Item 0 mismatch 6.)
146	- **[INFERRED]** **The no-generated-import rule is a kept isolation test**, not a property left
147	  to design. The test scans the runtime evidence and entry-source modules for any reference to a
148	  generated symbol and asserts none, and imports/constructs evidence with the generated package
149	  absent from the path. It is the only guard that keeps the concept's central
150	  runtime-independent-of-generated-classes bet from silently rotting. *(Orchestrator decision,
151	  agent-grade, 2026-07-12.)*
152	- **[INFERRED]** **Headline value is projected by a read-only normalization; the report artifact
153	  stays opaque and unmodified.** The projection layer *reads* the generated report's headline and
154	  normalizes only the value it writes onto the generic response key — it never mutates or rewrites
155	  the attached report, which stays opaque and byte-unchanged in evidence. The generated report
156	  uses underscore headlines (`all_satisfied`, `not_assessed`); `violation` and `indeterminate`
157	  already match. (Item 0 mismatch 5; `real_evaluator.py:189` `HEADLINE_TO_POLICY`, adapted from
158	  the spike's dict-rewrite to a read-only projection because production evidence holds the report
159	  opaque.) *(Orchestrator decision, agent-grade, 2026-07-12.)*
160	- **[INFERRED]** **The canonical evidence vocabulary is pinned in this item, runtime-owned:**
161	  `satisfied | violated | indeterminate | not_assessed` (underscore forms). The runtime owns its
162	  evidence surface; packages conform. **Ownership direction:** Item 9's contract conforms the
163	  *generated* side to the runtime's vocabulary, not the reverse — so the projection normalizes to
164	  a target fixed *here*, and SC2 is closable in Item 10 without waiting for Item 9. Item 9 must
165	  align the generated `ConstraintReport` headline vocabulary to this set. *(Orchestrator decision,
166	  agent-grade, 2026-07-12; resolves review L1-1/L1-2.)*
167	
168	### Normalized failure outcome
169	
170	- **[INHERITED]** **One normalized outcome for every evaluation failure**, carrying: phase,
171	  module or channel when known, cause, retryability, and partial-artifact status. (concept
172	  "Contracts and the Evaluator".)
173	- **[HARD]** **The `phase` field ranges over teax's real per-run phases**, in order:
174	  1. **`entry_validation`** — the typed entry input is rejected before any module runs
175	     (missing/extra/wrong-type). A genuinely distinct pre-execution phase.
176	  2. **`preparation`** — topology and write-handler validation. Runs **once at prepare**
177	     (`PipelineExecutor.build_graph` → `PipelineValidator.validate`,
178	     `pipeline_executor.py:104`), not per case; the write-handler-per-ExitPoint-type demand
179	     (`pipeline_validator.py:326`) and producer/declaration type-mismatch check
180	     (`pipeline_validator.py:~352`) live here. A whole study hits these once, not per candidate.
181	  3. **`module_execution`** — everything raised inside `module.run()` during the per-case run
182	     loop (`pipeline_executor.py:126–140`): an arbitrary module exception, a Pydantic
183	     `ValidationError` (generated modules validate inside `run()`), the aggregator's exact-schema
184	     rejecting a missing result, a `MultiOutput` missing field (`:205`), a field-extraction
185	     failure (`:397`). These are **one phase**, distinguished by `cause`, not by phase.
186	  4. **`output_write`** — writing artifacts on the file-backed path (never reached in no-persist
187	     mode).
188	- **[HARD]** **SC3's three distinguishable places, bound to the taxonomy:** a **module
189	  exception** is a `module_execution` failure; the **"schema failure"** SC3 means is the
190	  **pre-execution `entry_validation` rejection** — a real, separate phase from module execution;
191	  an **infeasible (`indeterminate`) verdict** is ordinary evidence, never a failure. An *in-run*
192	  schema failure (aggregator missing-field, Pydantic error inside `run()`) is **not** a separate
193	  phase — it is a `module_execution` failure carrying cause detail, matching the concept, which
194	  buckets "missing inputs, schema failures, thrown predicate code, or a missing aggregator field"
195	  together as execution failures (Required Invariants "Graph and Evaluation"). SC3's kept test
196	  exercises the `entry_validation` schema rejection, not the in-`run()` one.
197	- **[INHERITED]** **Violation stays evidence; breakage stays failure.** An assertion whose
198	  actual value differs from expected returns `violated` as evidence with ordinary outputs
199	  intact; a non-finite operand yields `indeterminate` as evidence. Only the `entry_validation`,
200	  `preparation`, `module_execution`, and `output_write` failures above are failures. (concept
201	  Required Invariants "Graph and Evaluation"; epic Item 10 success criterion.)
202	
203	### Package load
204	
205	- **[HARD]** **The sealed package loads under its declared package name.** The package's
206	  internal imports are absolute to its declared name (`from wi014_s4. …`), so the evaluator's
207	  package-load step must place/load it under that declared name, not its on-disk directory
208	  name. The canonical package-load protocol is **Item 9's** to own; Item 10 consumes it and
209	  must not hard-code a directory-name assumption. (Item 0 mismatch 8; `real_evaluator.py:load_package`.)
210	- **[INFERRED]** **Item 10 uses a provisional loader pending Item 9.** Item 9 has not landed, but
211	  Item 10 must load Item 0's package now to run any test — via the symlink-under-declared-name
212	  approach the spike uses (`real_evaluator.py:73`). "Item 9 owns the protocol" does **not** mean
213	  "Item 10 can't load anything yet"; the provisional loader is replaced when Item 9's protocol
214	  lands. *(Resolves review L3-3.)*
215	
216	## Implementation Prerequisites (not API requirements)
217	
218	These are sequencing/ops prerequisites for building the item, not contract obligations of the
219	evaluator API. Nothing about `MappingEntrySource`, `ModelEvidence`, or the failure outcome
220	depends on them — they belong to the plan, not the API surface.
221	
222	- **Provision teax's own venv as the first implementation step.** teax's own `.venv`/`uv run`
223	  is broken for real-simkit runs; the spikes borrowed the fusion-tea (a.k.a. agentic-mbse) venv
224	  with a `PYTHONPATH`/`sys.path` insert. Items 10–12 must stand up teax's own working environment
225	  before building on it. (epic Risks: "teax environment provisioning"; Item 0 / S5 Reproduction.)
226	
227	## Non-Goals
228	
229	- **Study semantics** — `StudyDefinition`, strategies, the runner, the SQLite store, atomic
230	  case commit, proposal records, and resume are Item 11. This item builds only the evaluator,
231	  entry source, evidence types, and failure outcome the runner calls into.
232	- **Optimizers and adaptive strategies** — deferred with S7.
233	- **Contract *authoring/sealing*** — `ModelContract`/`PackageContract` derivation and the seal
234	  are Item 9. Item 10 *consumes* the sealed package; it does not produce contracts.
235	- **Proposal validation** — deciding malformed/missing/wrong-type vs non-finite for *proposals*
236	  is Item 11's runner concern (Item 0 mismatches 2–3). Item 10 only guarantees its entry source
237	  does not itself misclassify non-finite input.
238	- **Canonical non-finite operand *encoding* in serialized evidence** — Item 0 flagged the
239	  observed-operand NaN JSON-encoding as a schema decision tagged to Item 11. Item 10 holds the
240	  report opaquely and does not freeze that on-disk encoding (see Open Questions).
241	
242	## Open Questions / Deferred to design
243	
244	### RESERVED — owner decision at design: `MappingEntrySource` API shape
245	
246	`[RESERVED: owner decision at design]` — Reid has reserved this choice. Both candidate shapes,
247	with consequences, captured here so design can execute the decision without re-deriving it. The
248	choice does **not** relax any requirement above: no silent coercion, and the wrong-type
249	diagnostic naming expected/got types, hold under either shape.
250	
251	- **Shape A — instantiated-models-only.** The source accepts already-constructed Pydantic
252	  entry models (e.g. a `ToyPlantParams` instance), as the S5 strict probe did.
253	  - *Consequence:* type correctness is guaranteed by construction; the caller (Item 11's
254	    strategy→candidate bridge) owns building the channel model from parameter-ID values, and
255	    that bridge is where the two-level mapping (channel → model; field → parameter ID) is
256	    resolved. Non-finite floats pass through automatically (non-strict float model).
257	  - *Consequence:* the wrong-type diagnostic fires at *bridge construction*, not inside the
258	    entry source; the source must still refuse an instance of the wrong channel model and name
259	    expected vs got.
260	- **Shape B — validate-raw-mappings.** The source accepts raw mappings and validates them into
261	  the declared entry channel model itself.
262	  - *Consequence:* the source owns the two-level resolution and the type validation, so the
263	    wrong-type diagnostic lives here; it must permit non-finite floats through validation (a
264	    strict model would reject `NaN`/`inf` and silently kill the indeterminate class).
265	  - *Consequence:* raw-mapping validation is closer to the file-backed loader's behavior, which
266	    may simplify backend parity — but requires an explicit "no coercion across parameter IDs"
267	    rule that Shape A gets for free.
268	  - *Consequence (weighs against the no-generated-import rule):* the declared entry channel model
269	    is a *generated* class (e.g. `ToyPlantParams`), obtained dynamically from the loaded package.
270	    To validate raw mappings *into* it, the Shape B source must reference that generated model
271	    shape at runtime. It is a dynamic dependency, not a static import, so the letter of
272	    "runtime types never import generated classes" is met — but the spirit is strained, and the
273	    isolation test above must be written to allow the dynamic lookup while still forbidding a
274	    static generated import. Under Shape A the caller builds the model and the source never
275	    touches a generated class. *(Resolves review L3-2.)*
276	- **Cross-cutting for either shape:** Item 0 mismatch 1 means the contract the source validates
277	  against is channel→model→field, so whichever shape is chosen, the design must define how a
278	  study variable ("vary `plant_budget`") selects a *field* of the entry channel model.
279	
280	### Deferred to design
281	
282	- **Provenance contents of `ModelEvidence`** — which fields (executable fingerprint, input
283	  digest, generator/runtime versions, timestamp) the provenance record carries. The concept
284	  says "provenance"; the exact set is a design decision, constrained by what Item 11's resume
285	  join needs (lineage + executable/study fingerprints + candidate identity).
286	- **Opaque-report storage form** — whether the "full report as opaque artifact" is held as the
287	  in-memory generated object, a serialized blob, or a content-addressed reference. Interacts
288	  with Item 11's store and with the deferred non-finite encoding decision; keep it opaque to
289	  runtime types either way.
290	- **Retryability classification** — which failure phases/causes are marked retryable vs
291	  terminal in the normalized outcome. The evaluator is deterministic per case, so most failures
292	  are not transiently retryable; design should state the rule rather than leave the field free.
293	- **Whether the ExitPoint-write-handler coupling is worked around or accepted** — the in-memory
294	  backend can either build the JSON router unconditionally (Item 0's approach) or the design can
295	  decouple validator-validity from ExitPoint-writability. A local fix here vs a validator change
296	  is a design call; note if it grows beyond Item 10.
297	
298	---
299	
300	## Related Artifacts
301	
302	- **Epic:** `.project/reference/epic_constraint_execution.md` — Item 10 (canonical:
303	  sysml-codegen `.project/backlog/epic_constraint_execution.md`).
304	- **Required Reading (from the epic):**
305	  - `.project/reference/constraint-execution-concept.md` — "Contracts and the Evaluator",

307	    carry-forwards.
308	  - `.project/active/spike-teax-typed-entry-scalar-continuity/findings.md` — S5 result and
309	    carry-forwards.
310	  - `.project/active/constraint-study-integration-spike/findings.md` — Item 0 findings; the
311	    eight named evaluator-interface mismatches.
312	- **Dependencies:** Item 0 (seam findings — landed); Item 9 (contract consumption + package-load
313	  protocol, and conforming the generated report's headline vocabulary to *this item's*
314	  runtime-owned canonical set — hardens this item when it lands; the vocabulary itself is pinned
315	  here, not by Item 9).
316	- **Design:** `.project/active/model-evaluator/design.md` (to be created).
317

What does not yet exist is the production runtime the study layer (Item 11) will build on: a
typed in-memory entry source, a prepared-pipeline backend with the file-backed path kept for
audit, an immutable evidence envelope that never depends on generated classes, and one
normalized failure outcome that keeps "the design is infeasible" (evidence) separate from
"the run broke" (failure). Item 0's eight mismatches are the concrete gap list: each is a
schema/naming/wiring detail the production API must resolve now, before Item 11 freezes its
store schema against this evaluator.

This item productionizes that seam. It is the teax half of the "Contracts and the Evaluator"
concept section; it does not build the study store, runner, strategies, or policy (Item 11+).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] **S5 invariants are kept teax tests:** mapping-vs-file case-level parity; pre-execution
  rejection of an invalid typed input (missing/extra/wrong-type) before any module runs;
  execution-context isolation across cases; and no output directory created when persistence is
  off.
- [ ] **S4-lineage packages evaluate to evidence:** evaluating a sealed generated package
  (Item 0's setup now; Item 9's sealed output when it lands) returns `ModelEvidence` whose
  constraint verdicts are projected onto generic response keys using the runtime-owned canonical
  vocabulary pinned in this item (`satisfied | violated | indeterminate | not_assessed`), with
  the full generated report attached as an opaque artifact and no generated class imported by
  any runtime type. This is closable in Item 10 — the vocabulary is pinned here, not deferred to
  Item 9.
- [ ] **Runtime never depends on generated classes (kept isolation test):** an import scan of
  the runtime evidence and entry-source modules finds no reference to any generated symbol; the
  modules import and construct evidence with the generated package absent from the path.
- [ ] **Three phases are distinguishable:** a module exception, a schema-validation rejection
  at entry (`entry_validation` phase), and an infeasible (`indeterminate`) verdict land in three
  distinguishable places — the first two as the normalized failure outcome with different
  phase/cause (`module_execution` vs `entry_validation`), the third as ordinary evidence, never
  a failure.
- [ ] **Non-finite input reaches the verdict, not the guard:** a well-formed candidate with a
  non-finite value (e.g. a NaN budget) passes entry validation and evaluates to
  `indeterminate` — it is never rejected as invalid input.
- [ ] **Both backends agree (kept parity test):** the prepared in-memory backend and the
  file-backed backend return the equivalent-class-equal result (defined in Known Requirements)
  for the same canonical inputs, with the NaN/indeterminate case in the fixture set.
- [ ] S5's `RootModel[float]` continuity regression test is committed — **already discharged
  this run** (S5 carry-forward (1)); recorded here as done, not re-planned.

## Known Requirements

Grading note: items forced by how the *real* generated package and TEAx validator actually
behave (named by Item 0) are `[HARD]`; design intents carried from the owner-ratified concept
and epic are `[INHERITED]` with their source cited. See `capture-fidelity.md`.

### Typed entry source (`MappingEntrySource`)

- **[HARD]** Typed entry is **two-level, not a flat parameter-ID→scalar map.** The real
  EntryPoint emits one structured channel (`toy_plant_params: ToyPlantParams`) whose *fields*
  are the contract parameter IDs; downstream modules field-extract
  (`toy_plant_params.toy_plant__Toy_Plant__plant_budget`). The entry source must express the
  contract at both levels — channel → model, and model field → parameter ID — not as a single
  flat map keyed by parameter ID. (Item 0 mismatch 1; `real_evaluator.py:evaluate`.)
- **[INHERITED]** **No silent coercion under any shape.** A value must never be accepted under
  a mismatched contract parameter ID. (concept "Contracts and the Evaluator"; S5 findings
  Open Questions.)
- **[INHERITED]** **An invalid typed input is rejected before any module executes, with a
  diagnostic naming expected and got types.** "Invalid" means missing, extra, or wrong-type.
  The rejection happens before the first module runs and names both the expected type and the
  type actually supplied. **Which layer performs the rejection is exactly the reserved choice**
  (see Open Questions): under a validate-raw source it is the entry source at field-value
  granularity; under an instantiated-models source the source rejects a wrong *channel-model*
  and the field-value check lives at the Item 11 bridge. The requirement — rejected
  pre-execution, expected-and-got named — holds identically under both shapes; it is the study
  layer's first line of defense, required behavior, not spike detail. (concept Appendix B, S5
  carry-forward (3).)
- **[HARD]** **Non-finite floats are well-formed input, not invalid input.** Entry validation
  rejects missing, extra, and wrong-*type* inputs before execution (at whichever layer the
  reserved choice places it), but must let a non-finite float (`NaN`, `inf`) through — it is a
  well-formed candidate that the generated Kleene predicate evaluates to `indeterminate`. Conflating non-finite with invalid would make the
  entire indeterminate verdict class unreachable through typed entry. (Item 0 mismatches 1–2;
  the real `ToyPlantParams` is a non-strict float model that accepts non-finite values.)

### Prepared-pipeline backend and the file-backed path

- **[INHERITED]** **Prepare once, fresh context per case.** Validate and build the pipeline
  topology a single time; each case evaluates in its own fresh execution context. (concept;
  S5.) Prepare-once measured ~64× faster than rebuild-per-case on the real package (Item 0
  benchmark; ~4× on S5's toy graph — the speedup scales with model-validation cost).
- **[INHERITED]** **The file-backed path is retained for auditable runs**, producing the same
  evidence plus persisted artifacts. (concept "How It Works — Evaluate One Design Point".)
- **[INHERITED]** **Case-level parity between the two backends is a kept test**, over an
  explicit equivalence class; a faster backend is admitted only on that parity. (concept;
  Required Invariant "auditable and fast evaluators return equivalent … results".) The
  equivalence class:
  - **Compared:** selected outputs, matched by stable ID, with **NaN-aware numeric equality** —
    two values are equal if they are numerically equal *or* both non-finite of the same kind
    (both NaN counts equal; `+inf`≡`+inf`, `-inf`≡`-inf`). Constraint verdict statuses are
    compared **exactly** (string equality on the canonical vocabulary).
  - **Excluded (enumerated):** provenance, timestamps, input digests, artifact paths, and the
    opaque report's on-disk encoding — the file-backed path serializes and the in-memory path
    does not, so byte-level report form is not a parity field.
  - **The NaN / indeterminate case MUST be in the parity fixture set.** It is the case the whole
    architecture exists to preserve, and it is exactly where a naive field compare fails: the
    file-backed path round-trips a NaN through JSON while the in-memory path holds a real
    `float('nan')`, and `NaN != NaN`. The NaN-aware rule above is what makes the two agree.
- **[INHERITED]** **No-persist mode writes nothing** — no output directory is created when
  persistence is off. (S5 findings; concept.)
- **[HARD]** **The validator requires ExitPoint write handlers even in no-persist mode.** A
  pure in-memory evaluator that never writes still must build an output router with JSON write
  handlers for the generated custom types, because `PipelineValidator` demands a write handler
  per ExitPoint output type unconditionally (validity coupled to writability). The in-memory
  backend must construct that router (or the design must decouple validity from writability).
  (Item 0 mismatch 7; `real_evaluator.py:_build_prepared`.)
- **[HARD]** **Evaluator protocol is `evaluate(typed_inputs) -> Evidence`** — it carries no
  `attempt_number`. The prepared pipeline is deterministic and stateless per case; the spike's
  `attempt_number` argument was unused. Retry/attempt bookkeeping belongs to the runner
  (Item 11), not the evaluator protocol. (Item 0 mismatch 4; `real_evaluator.py:evaluate`.)

### `ModelEvidence`

- **[INHERITED]** **Immutable, runtime-owned generic envelope.** `ModelEvidence` carries:
  response entries keyed by stable IDs (constraint verdicts project onto generic response
  keys), selected outputs, provenance, and the full generated report attached as an opaque
  model artifact. (concept "Contracts and the Evaluator".)
- **[INHERITED]** **Runtime types never import generated classes.** The evidence envelope and
  every other runtime type depend only on generic/runtime types; the generated
  `ConstraintReport` is held opaquely, never imported. Item 0 confirmed the generic projection
  is clean. (concept; Item 0 mismatch 6.)
- **[INFERRED]** **The no-generated-import rule is a kept isolation test**, not a property left
  to design. The test scans the runtime evidence and entry-source modules for any reference to a
  generated symbol and asserts none, and imports/constructs evidence with the generated package
  absent from the path. It is the only guard that keeps the concept's central
  runtime-independent-of-generated-classes bet from silently rotting. *(Orchestrator decision,
  agent-grade, 2026-07-12.)*
- **[INFERRED]** **Headline value is projected by a read-only normalization; the report artifact
  stays opaque and unmodified.** The projection layer *reads* the generated report's headline and
  normalizes only the value it writes onto the generic response key — it never mutates or rewrites
  the attached report, which stays opaque and byte-unchanged in evidence. The generated report
  uses underscore headlines (`all_satisfied`, `not_assessed`); `violation` and `indeterminate`
  already match. (Item 0 mismatch 5; `real_evaluator.py:189` `HEADLINE_TO_POLICY`, adapted from
  the spike's dict-rewrite to a read-only projection because production evidence holds the report
  opaque.) *(Orchestrator decision, agent-grade, 2026-07-12.)*
- **[INFERRED]** **The canonical evidence vocabulary is pinned in this item, runtime-owned:**
  `satisfied | violated | indeterminate | not_assessed` (underscore forms). The runtime owns its
  evidence surface; packages conform. **Ownership direction:** Item 9's contract conforms the
  *generated* side to the runtime's vocabulary, not the reverse — so the projection normalizes to
  a target fixed *here*, and SC2 is closable in Item 10 without waiting for Item 9. Item 9 must
  align the generated `ConstraintReport` headline vocabulary to this set. *(Orchestrator decision,
  agent-grade, 2026-07-12; resolves review L1-1/L1-2.)*

### Normalized failure outcome

- **[INHERITED]** **One normalized outcome for every evaluation failure**, carrying: phase,
  module or channel when known, cause, retryability, and partial-artifact status. (concept
  "Contracts and the Evaluator".)
- **[HARD]** **The `phase` field ranges over teax's real per-run phases**, in order:
  1. **`entry_validation`** — the typed entry input is rejected before any module runs
     (missing/extra/wrong-type). A genuinely distinct pre-execution phase.
  2. **`preparation`** — topology and write-handler validation. Runs **once at prepare**
     (`PipelineExecutor.build_graph` → `PipelineValidator.validate`,
     `pipeline_executor.py:104`), not per case; the write-handler-per-ExitPoint-type demand
     (`pipeline_validator.py:326`) and producer/declaration type-mismatch check
     (`pipeline_validator.py:~352`) live here. A whole study hits these once, not per candidate.
  3. **`module_execution`** — everything raised inside `module.run()` during the per-case run
     loop (`pipeline_executor.py:126–140`): an arbitrary module exception, a Pydantic
     `ValidationError` (generated modules validate inside `run()`), the aggregator's exact-schema
     rejecting a missing result, a `MultiOutput` missing field (`:205`), a field-extraction
     failure (`:397`). These are **one phase**, distinguished by `cause`, not by phase.
  4. **`output_write`** — writing artifacts on the file-backed path (never reached in no-persist
     mode).
- **[HARD]** **SC3's three distinguishable places, bound to the taxonomy:** a **module
  exception** is a `module_execution` failure; the **"schema failure"** SC3 means is the
  **pre-execution `entry_validation` rejection** — a real, separate phase from module execution;
  an **infeasible (`indeterminate`) verdict** is ordinary evidence, never a failure. An *in-run*
  schema failure (aggregator missing-field, Pydantic error inside `run()`) is **not** a separate
  phase — it is a `module_execution` failure carrying cause detail, matching the concept, which
  buckets "missing inputs, schema failures, thrown predicate code, or a missing aggregator field"
  together as execution failures (Required Invariants "Graph and Evaluation"). SC3's kept test
  exercises the `entry_validation` schema rejection, not the in-`run()` one.
- **[INHERITED]** **Violation stays evidence; breakage stays failure.** An assertion whose
  actual value differs from expected returns `violated` as evidence with ordinary outputs
  intact; a non-finite operand yields `indeterminate` as evidence. Only the `entry_validation`,
  `preparation`, `module_execution`, and `output_write` failures above are failures. (concept
  Required Invariants "Graph and Evaluation"; epic Item 10 success criterion.)

### Package load

- **[HARD]** **The sealed package loads under its declared package name.** The package's
  internal imports are absolute to its declared name (`from wi014_s4. …`), so the evaluator's
  package-load step must place/load it under that declared name, not its on-disk directory
  name. The canonical package-load protocol is **Item 9's** to own; Item 10 consumes it and
  must not hard-code a directory-name assumption. (Item 0 mismatch 8; `real_evaluator.py:load_package`.)
- **[INFERRED]** **Item 10 uses a provisional loader pending Item 9.** Item 9 has not landed, but
  Item 10 must load Item 0's package now to run any test — via the symlink-under-declared-name
  approach the spike uses (`real_evaluator.py:73`). "Item 9 owns the protocol" does **not** mean
  "Item 10 can't load anything yet"; the provisional loader is replaced when Item 9's protocol
  lands. *(Resolves review L3-3.)*

## Implementation Prerequisites (not API requirements)

These are sequencing/ops prerequisites for building the item, not contract obligations of the
evaluator API. Nothing about `MappingEntrySource`, `ModelEvidence`, or the failure outcome
depends on them — they belong to the plan, not the API surface.

- **Provision teax's own venv as the first implementation step.** teax's own `.venv`/`uv run`
  is broken for real-simkit runs; the spikes borrowed the fusion-tea (a.k.a. agentic-mbse) venv
  with a `PYTHONPATH`/`sys.path` insert. Items 10–12 must stand up teax's own working environment
  before building on it. (epic Risks: "teax environment provisioning"; Item 0 / S5 Reproduction.)

## Non-Goals

- **Study semantics** — `StudyDefinition`, strategies, the runner, the SQLite store, atomic
  case commit, proposal records, and resume are Item 11. This item builds only the evaluator,
  entry source, evidence types, and failure outcome the runner calls into.
- **Optimizers and adaptive strategies** — deferred with S7.
- **Contract *authoring/sealing*** — `ModelContract`/`PackageContract` derivation and the seal
  are Item 9. Item 10 *consumes* the sealed package; it does not produce contracts.
- **Proposal validation** — deciding malformed/missing/wrong-type vs non-finite for *proposals*
  is Item 11's runner concern (Item 0 mismatches 2–3). Item 10 only guarantees its entry source
  does not itself misclassify non-finite input.
- **Canonical non-finite operand *encoding* in serialized evidence** — Item 0 flagged the
  observed-operand NaN JSON-encoding as a schema decision tagged to Item 11. Item 10 holds the
  report opaquely and does not freeze that on-disk encoding (see Open Questions).

## Open Questions / Deferred to design

### RESERVED — owner decision at design: `MappingEntrySource` API shape

`[RESERVED: owner decision at design]` — Reid has reserved this choice. Both candidate shapes,
with consequences, captured here so design can execute the decision without re-deriving it. The
choice does **not** relax any requirement above: no silent coercion, and the wrong-type
diagnostic naming expected/got types, hold under either shape.

- **Shape A — instantiated-models-only.** The source accepts already-constructed Pydantic
  entry models (e.g. a `ToyPlantParams` instance), as the S5 strict probe did.
  - *Consequence:* type correctness is guaranteed by construction; the caller (Item 11's
    strategy→candidate bridge) owns building the channel model from parameter-ID values, and
    that bridge is where the two-level mapping (channel → model; field → parameter ID) is
    resolved. Non-finite floats pass through automatically (non-strict float model).
  - *Consequence:* the wrong-type diagnostic fires at *bridge construction*, not inside the
    entry source; the source must still refuse an instance of the wrong channel model and name
    expected vs got.
- **Shape B — validate-raw-mappings.** The source accepts raw mappings and validates them into
  the declared entry channel model itself.
  - *Consequence:* the source owns the two-level resolution and the type validation, so the
    wrong-type diagnostic lives here; it must permit non-finite floats through validation (a
    strict model would reject `NaN`/`inf` and silently kill the indeterminate class).
  - *Consequence:* raw-mapping validation is closer to the file-backed loader's behavior, which
    may simplify backend parity — but requires an explicit "no coercion across parameter IDs"
    rule that Shape A gets for free.
  - *Consequence (weighs against the no-generated-import rule):* the declared entry channel model
    is a *generated* class (e.g. `ToyPlantParams`), obtained dynamically from the loaded package.
    To validate raw mappings *into* it, the Shape B source must reference that generated model
    shape at runtime. It is a dynamic dependency, not a static import, so the letter of
    "runtime types never import generated classes" is met — but the spirit is strained, and the
    isolation test above must be written to allow the dynamic lookup while still forbidding a
    static generated import. Under Shape A the caller builds the model and the source never
    touches a generated class. *(Resolves review L3-2.)*
- **Cross-cutting for either shape:** Item 0 mismatch 1 means the contract the source validates
  against is channel→model→field, so whichever shape is chosen, the design must define how a
  study variable ("vary `plant_budget`") selects a *field* of the entry channel model.

### Deferred to design

- **Provenance contents of `ModelEvidence`** — which fields (executable fingerprint, input
  digest, generator/runtime versions, timestamp) the provenance record carries. The concept
  says "provenance"; the exact set is a design decision, constrained by what Item 11's resume
  join needs (lineage + executable/study fingerprints + candidate identity).
- **Opaque-report storage form** — whether the "full report as opaque artifact" is held as the
  in-memory generated object, a serialized blob, or a content-addressed reference. Interacts
  with Item 11's store and with the deferred non-finite encoding decision; keep it opaque to
  runtime types either way.
- **Retryability classification** — which failure phases/causes are marked retryable vs
  terminal in the normalized outcome. The evaluator is deterministic per case, so most failures
  are not transiently retryable; design should state the rule rather than leave the field free.
- **Whether the ExitPoint-write-handler coupling is worked around or accepted** — the in-memory
  backend can either build the JSON router unconditionally (Item 0's approach) or the design can
  decouple validator-validity from ExitPoint-writability. A local fix here vs a validator change
  is a design call; note if it grows beyond Item 10.

---

## Related Artifacts

- **Epic:** `.project/reference/epic_constraint_execution.md` — Item 10 (canonical:
  sysml-codegen `.project/backlog/epic_constraint_execution.md`).
- **Required Reading (from the epic):**
  - `.project/reference/constraint-execution-concept.md` — "Contracts and the Evaluator",
    Required Invariants (Graph and Evaluation; Study Execution), Appendix B S5 result +
    carry-forwards.
  - `.project/active/spike-teax-typed-entry-scalar-continuity/findings.md` — S5 result and
    carry-forwards.
  - `.project/active/constraint-study-integration-spike/findings.md` — Item 0 findings; the
    eight named evaluator-interface mismatches.
- **Dependencies:** Item 0 (seam findings — landed); Item 9 (contract consumption + package-load
  protocol, and conforming the generated report's headline vocabulary to *this item's*
  runtime-owned canonical set — hardens this item when it lands; the vocabulary itself is pinned
  here, not by Item 9).
- **Design:** `.project/active/model-evaluator/design.md` (to be created).

---

**Next Steps:** After approval, proceed to `/_my_spec_review` (fresh session), then
`/_my_design`. Design must resolve the reserved `MappingEntrySource` shape with the owner.

55

57	around the unchanged teax executor. It has two lifecycle steps that already exist in the
58	runtime: **prepare once** (validate topology, build the graph, register write handlers) and
59	**evaluate per case** (set typed entry channels into a fresh context, run, project the result).
60	
61	The one hard rule that shapes everything: **runtime evidence and entry types never depend on
62	generated classes.** The generated `ConstraintReport` is held opaque — read by duck-typed
63	attribute access at projection time, never imported, never mutated. This is what lets Item 11
64	freeze a store schema against `ModelEvidence` without ever seeing a generated symbol, and it is
65	enforced by a kept isolation test, not left to discipline.
66	
67	Three outcomes must stay distinguishable, and the runtime already separates them: an infeasible
68	design is **evidence** (`indeterminate` verdict, ordinary outputs intact); a broken run is a
69	**failure** (normalized outcome carrying phase + cause); and a malformed candidate is rejected
70	**before any module runs** (`entry_validation` phase). The evaluator's whole job is to preserve
71	that separation across the seam from the generated package into runtime-owned types.

73	We build from the Item 0 probe's proven shape and change exactly what the spec requires:

116	  `projection.py` are generated-import-clean and construct with the generated package absent;
117	  `evaluator.py` and `package_load.py` legitimately touch the package and are excluded from the
118	  isolation scan by design. *Rejected: putting these in `core/` — `core/` is pipeline
119	  orchestration, evaluation is a distinct layer on top, and a dedicated package makes the
120	  isolation-scan target crisp.*
121	- **D3. Evaluator protocol is `evaluate(typed_inputs: Mapping[str, BaseModel]) -> ModelEvidence`;
122	  no `attempt_number`.** *Rejected: carrying `attempt_number` (the probe did, unused) — retry
123	  bookkeeping is the runner's, and the prepared pipeline is stateless per case (Item 0 mismatch 4).*
124	- **D4. Failure surfaces as a raised `EvaluationFailed` carrying an immutable `EvaluationFailure`;
125	  `retryable` is always `False` for evaluator failures.** The evaluator raises, the runner
126	  catches and commits the case; a raise (not a return-union) matches S6's runner control flow.
127	  *Rejected: a `Result[ModelEvidence, EvaluationFailure]` return union — it would force every
128	  caller to branch and diverges from the S6 runner the seam is validated against; and a
129	  free-form `retryable` field — the rule is fixed (deterministic → terminal), so we state it,
130	  not leave it open (spec deferred item 3).* **Retryability is a decision, not a bet:** no failure
131	  the evaluator raises is transiently retryable, because a deterministic function fails the same
132	  way every time; transient/infra retry is the runner's layer (S6's `RetryableError`), never the
133	  evaluator's, so `retryable=False` is fixed here by construction.
134	- **D5. In-memory backend builds the JSON router unconditionally (local workaround), not a
135	  validator change.** `create_output_router_with_json_schemas(generated_type_names,
136	  in_memory=True)`. *Rejected: decoupling validator-validity from ExitPoint-writability — that
137	  touches shared validation semantics other pipelines rely on, is out of Item 10 scope, and the
138	  workaround is a three-line construction. **Flag:** if a later item needs a genuinely
139	  handler-free in-memory validation path, revisit the `pipeline_validator.py:326` coupling then
140	  (spec deferred item 4; Item 0 mismatch 7).*
141	- **D6. Headline normalization is a read-only projection onto the runtime-owned canonical
142	  vocabulary `satisfied | violated | indeterminate | not_assessed` (underscore).** The
143	  projection reads the generated report's headline and writes a normalized value onto the
144	  generic response key; the attached report stays opaque and byte-unchanged. *Rejected:
145	  normalizing to S6's hyphen policy vocabulary (`all-satisfied`, the probe's `HEADLINE_TO_POLICY`)
146	  — Item 10 owns the evidence surface and pins the underscore set here; packages conform (Item 9
147	  aligns the generated side later). Also rejected: the probe's dict-rewrite of the report —
148	  production holds it opaque (spec `ModelEvidence` section, review L1-1/L1-2).*
149	- **D7. Package loading is a `PackageLoader` seam; Item 10 ships a provisional
150	  symlink-under-declared-name loader that verifies the seal.** *Rejected: hard-coding the
151	  on-disk directory name — the package's internal imports are absolute to its declared name
152	  (`from wi014_s4. …`), Item 9 owns the canonical protocol, and the seam lets Item 9 swap in
153	  without touching the evaluator (Item 0 mismatch 8; spec package-load section).*
154	
155	## Architecture
156	
157	Three layers, generated-package dependency increasing outward:
158	
159	```
160	  candidate values ──(Item 11 bridge, out of scope)──▶ typed entry models
161	        │
162	        ▼
163	  MappingEntrySource.validate(values)                 [entry_source.py — isolation-clean]
164	        │  refuses wrong channel-model instance (expected vs got); non-finite passes
165	        ▼
166	  PreparedEvaluator.evaluate(typed_inputs)            [evaluator.py — touches package]
167	        │  fresh context → override _execute_entry → executor.run(persist=False)
168	        ▼
169	  project(run_result, opaque_report)                  [projection.py — duck-typed, isolation-clean]
170	        │  read-only headline normalize; report held opaque
171	        ▼
172	  ModelEvidence(responses, outputs, provenance, report)   [evidence.py — isolation-clean]
173	```
174	
175	**Prepare once (study startup):** `PreparedEvaluator(loader, spec_path)` calls the loader
176	(verify seal → load package under declared name → executable fingerprint), builds the schema
177	registry / entry loaders / in-memory JSON router from the package's `CUSTOM_SCHEMA_TYPES`,
178	`build_graph(spec)` (validates topology — the `preparation` phase runs here, once), and derives
179	the `MappingEntrySource` from the EntryPoint's declared channel→type bindings.
180	
181	**Evaluate per case:** validate typed inputs against the source → build a fresh
182	`PipelineExecutionContext` seeded with those channel values → `run(graph, context,
183	persist_outputs=False)` → project. The executor subclass overrides only `_execute_entry` to read
184	from the seeded context instead of loading files (`real_evaluator.py` `MappingExecutor`).
185	
186	**File-backed backend (audit):** the standard `execute_pipeline` path — file entry, real router,
187	`persist_outputs=True` — then the *same* `project(...)`. It produces the same evidence plus
188	persisted artifacts. Both backends share projection and vocabulary; the parity test is what
189	admits the fast in-memory path.
190	
191	**Data flow into evidence.** `ModelEvidence` carries: `responses` (stable-ID-keyed entries —
192	per-constraint verdict statuses, already canonical, plus the normalized headline), `outputs`
193	(selected numeric outputs, unwrapped from `RootModel[float]`), `provenance` (see D-below), and
194	`report` (the opaque generated object, held as `Any`, never introspected by runtime types).
195	
196	## Required Invariants
197	
198	- **INV1. The four isolation-clean modules import only from an allowlist (stdlib, `pydantic`,
199	  `simkit`-internal) — checked by a static AST source scan including `TYPE_CHECKING` blocks — and
200	  each imports and constructs with the generated package absent from the path.** (Kept isolation
201	  test; two legs, allowlist not blacklist.)
202	- **INV2. Entry validation rejects missing / extra / wrong channel-model instances before the
203	  first module runs, naming expected and got; a non-finite float is never rejected.**
204	- **INV3. `prepare` runs topology + write-handler validation exactly once; `evaluate` never
205	  re-validates topology.**
206	- **INV4. Same (typed inputs, executable fingerprint) → equal evidence under the parity
207	  equivalence class** (selected outputs NaN-aware-equal; verdict statuses string-exact;
208	  provenance/timestamps/digests/artifact-paths/report-encoding excluded).
209	- **INV5. An `indeterminate` verdict is always evidence, never a failure; the four failure
210	  phases (`entry_validation`, `preparation`, `module_execution`, `output_write`) are the only
211	  failures.**
212	- **INV6. No output directory is created when `persist_outputs=False`.**
213	
214	## Component Overview
215	
216	`simkit/evaluation/` (new subpackage):
217	
218	- **`evidence.py`** *(isolation-clean).* `ModelEvidence` (frozen), `ResponseEntry`,
219	  `EvidenceProvenance`, and `CANONICAL_HEADLINE` vocabulary constant. Runtime-owned, depends only
220	  on generic types. Public.
221	- **`entry_source.py`** *(isolation-clean).* `MappingEntrySource` (Shape A) — `from_spec`
222	  derives expected channel→type map from the EntryPoint bindings; `validate` refuses wrong
223	  channel-model instance / missing / extra, naming expected vs got. Ported from
224	  `real_evaluator.py` `MappingEntrySource`, unchanged in shape. Public.
225	- **`failure.py`** *(isolation-clean).* `EvaluationPhase` enum (`entry_validation | preparation |
226	  module_execution | output_write`), `EvaluationFailure` (frozen: phase, cause, module_or_channel,
227	  retryable, partial_artifacts), `EvaluationFailed` exception carrying it. Public.
228	- **`projection.py`** *(isolation-clean, duck-typed).* `project(run_result, report) ->
229	  ModelEvidence` — read-only headline normalization, per-constraint status pass-through, output
230	  unwrap, opaque report attach. Reads the report by attribute; never imports it.
231	- **`evaluator.py`** *(touches package).* `Evaluator` protocol, `PreparedEvaluator` (in-memory,
232	  prepare-once), `FileBackedEvaluator` (audit). Ports `real_evaluator.py` `_build_prepared` /
233	  `RealPreparedEvaluator`, minus `attempt_number`, minus dict-rewrite. Public.
234	- **`package_load.py`** *(touches package).* `PackageLoader` protocol, `ProvisionalPackageLoader`
235	  (symlink-under-declared-name + inlined seal verification, from `real_evaluator.py:verify_seal`/
236	  `load_package`). Public, provisional pending Item 9.
237	
238	**Public API** (`simkit/evaluation/__init__.py`): `MappingEntrySource`, `ModelEvidence`,
239	`ResponseEntry`, `EvidenceProvenance`, `CANONICAL_HEADLINE`, `EvaluationPhase`,
240	`EvaluationFailure`, `EvaluationFailed`, `Evaluator`, `PreparedEvaluator`, `FileBackedEvaluator`,
241	`PackageLoader`, `ProvisionalPackageLoader`.
242	
243	### Deferred-item decisions (recorded)
244	
245	- **Provenance fields** (`EvidenceProvenance`): `executable_fingerprint` (from the seal),
246	  `evidence_schema_version` (runtime-owned; Item 11 binds compatibility on it), `evaluator_version`,
247	  and `input_digest` (canonical-serialized content hash of the typed inputs — a cross-check anchor
248	  for the resume join). *Deliberately excluded:* `study_id`, `candidate_id`, `proposal_id`,
249	  `strategy_*`, wall-clock timestamp — those are runner-owned (S6 `Compatibility` / three-layer
250	  identity) and stamping them here would break B2's determinism. **The harder reason candidate
251	  identity must stay out:** Item 0's deliberate replicate produced distinct `candidate_id`s with
252	  identical inputs sharing *one* content-addressed artifact — if evidence carried `candidate_id`,
253	  two replicates could not share one artifact, so exclusion is *required* by the store's
254	  content-addressed dedup, not merely determinism-friendly. Auditability is preserved through the
255	  runner's own identity record plus `input_digest` as a cross-check anchor. The evaluator is
256	  study-agnostic; Item 11 wraps evidence with its own identity. *(Resolves spec deferred item 1.)*
257	- **Opaque-report storage form:** held as the **in-memory generated object** (`Any`), never
258	  introspected. The file-backed path serializes it to JSON for its persisted artifact, but that
259	  encoding is excluded from parity and does not freeze Item 11's non-finite on-disk decision.
260	  *Rejected: serialize-at-evaluate (forces the deferred non-finite encoding now) or
261	  content-addressed reference (needs a store — that's Item 11).* *(Resolves spec deferred item 2.)*
262	- **Retryability rule:** every evaluator-raised `EvaluationFailure` is `retryable=False`. The
263	  evaluator is deterministic per case (B2; D4); transient/infra retry lives in the runner. State
264	  the rule; don't leave the field free. *(Resolves spec deferred item 3.)*
265	- **ExitPoint-write-handler coupling:** local workaround (D5). *(Resolves spec deferred item 4.)*
266	
267	## Non-Goals
268	
269	- **Study store, runner, strategies, policy, resume, atomic commit** — Item 11.
270	- **Contract authoring / sealing** (`ModelContract`/`PackageContract`) — Item 9. Item 10
271	  *consumes* the sealed package.
272	- **Proposal validation** (malformed vs non-finite for *proposals*) — Item 11's runner.
273	- **Canonical non-finite operand encoding in serialized evidence** — Item 11; the report stays
274	  opaque here.
275	- **Canonical package-load protocol** — Item 9; Item 10 uses the provisional loader.
276	
277	## Implementation Notes
278	
279	- **Phase → real failure map** (the taxonomy, bound to teax):
280	  - `entry_validation` — `MappingEntrySource.validate` raises (missing/extra/wrong channel-model).
281	    Pre-execution, a genuinely distinct phase. **This is the "schema failure" SC3 exercises.**
282	  - `preparation` — `build_graph`→`validate` at prepare (write-handler, producer/declaration
283	    mismatch, `pipeline_validator.py:326,~352`). Once per study, aborts before any case.
284	  - `module_execution` — anything raised during the per-case run loop
285	    (`pipeline_executor.py:126–140`): an arbitrary exception or Pydantic `ValidationError` inside
286	    `module.run()`, plus the executor-wrapper raises around it while gathering inputs / decomposing
287	    outputs — MultiOutput missing field (`:205`), single-output shape mismatch (`:226`),
288	    field-extraction `AttributeError`→`PipelineExecutionError` (`:397`), None-on-Optional (`:404`).
289	    **One phase, distinguished by `cause`, not phase** — an in-run-loop schema failure is *not* a
290	    separate phase.
291	  - `output_write` — file-backed persistence only; never reached in no-persist mode.
292	- **The evaluator catches executor exceptions and normalizes them**, replacing the probe's
293	  `except Exception → ExecutionFailed(str)` (`real_evaluator.py:evaluate`) with a mapping to
294	  `EvaluationFailure(phase=module_execution, cause=type+message, module_or_channel=<key when
295	  known>, retryable=False, partial_artifacts=none)`.
296	- **`input_digest` uses a stable non-finite tag** (`{"__nonfinite__": "nan"}`, from
297	  `real_evaluator.py:_json_safe`) *inside the digest only* — this is not the on-disk evidence
298	  encoding (Item 11's to freeze), just a deterministic hash input.
299	- **Projection code snippet (shape, not implementation):**
300	  ```python
301	  def project(result, report) -> ModelEvidence:            # report: opaque, duck-typed
302	      headline = CANONICAL_HEADLINE[report.headline]        # read-only normalize
303	      responses = {r.constraint_id: r.status for r in report.results}  # already canonical
304	      outputs = {k: v.root for k, v in selected(result)}    # RootModel[float] unwrap
305	      return ModelEvidence(responses={**responses, "headline": headline},
306	                           outputs=outputs, provenance=..., report=report)
307	  ```
308	- **Non-finite must survive to the verdict.** Do not add strict-float validation anywhere on the
309	  entry path (INV2, B3). The isolation and NaN-parity tests guard this.
310	- **Parity fixtures and non-finite handling.** What each leg can carry, stated precisely:
311	  - *In-memory leg* holds a real `float('nan')` end to end — entry values are constructed Pydantic
312	    models, never serialized.
313	  - *File-backed leg* mechanically round-trips a bare `NaN`/`Infinity` JSON token: `read_json_model`
314	    uses `json.load` (`readers.py:35`) and `write_json_model` uses `json.dump(model_dump(
315	    mode="json"))` (`writers.py:25–27`), both at stdlib `allow_nan=True` default, so a hand-authored
316	    entry file with a bare `NaN` token loads into the non-strict `ToyPlantParams` as `float('nan')`.
317	    Use the bare token, **not** the `{"__nonfinite__": …}` tag (that tag is digest-input only).
318	  - *Reconciliation with Item 0.* Item 0's "a NaN budget cannot travel through the file-backed JSON
319	    entry" is about the study **proposal/store** path (Item 11's higher layer), not the raw
320	    reader/writer a parity fixture uses. Both are true at their own layer; the earlier design
321	    hardened the concept's rationale without this distinction — corrected here.
322	  - *Two mandatory fixtures, and what each actually proves:*
323	    - **F-budget (budget = NaN → `indeterminate`).** NaN is confined to the constraint predicate
324	      operand, which lives in the *excluded* opaque report; the compared outputs `area` (= 12) and
325	      `cost` (= 3000) are finite (budget feeds only `cost ≤ budget`, not the numeric graph), and the
326	      verdict is the string `"indeterminate"`. **This proves indeterminate-verdict + finite-output
327	      parity across a NaN input — it does *not* exercise NaN-aware numeric output equality** (no
328	      compared field is ever non-finite). Keep it; name what it tests.
329	    - **F-output (plant_length = NaN → `area` = NaN, `cost` = NaN).** A non-finite input propagates
330	      to *compared numeric outputs*. Both legs produce non-finite `area`/`cost` (the file-backed leg
331	      carries the bare `NaN` token), so **this fixture exercises NaN-aware numeric output equality
332	      directly** — the compared field is non-finite on both sides and a naive `NaN != NaN` compare
333	      would spuriously fail without the rule. Verdict is also `indeterminate`.
334	  - *Scope of the cross-leg parity claim.* The NaN-aware rule is exercised on **file-expressible
335	    candidates** (bare `NaN`/`inf` tokens through stdlib json); both ToyPlant fixtures are
336	    file-expressible, so cross-leg parity holds directly. If a future backend cannot serialize a
337	    given non-finite candidate, parity for it is proven on the in-memory leg against a stated
338	    expectation only, and the cross-leg claim is scoped to file-expressible candidates — said
339	    explicitly rather than implied.
340	
341	## Potential Risks
342	
343	- **Isolation rot via a convenience import.** Someone adds `from wi014_s4 import ...` to
344	  `projection.py` for a type hint. *Mitigation:* INV1 kept test (import scan + package-absent
345	  construction) fails the build.
346	- **Provenance under-serves Item 11's resume join.** If Item 11 needs a field we omitted.
347	  *Mitigation:* fields chosen against S6's `Compatibility` row and the resume-join constraint
348	  (lineage + executable/study fingerprints + candidate identity); the evaluator-owned subset is
349	  small and additive-safe.
350	- **Parity test written naively fails on NaN.** *Mitigation:* the NaN-aware equality rule, plus a
351	  fixture (F-output) whose *compared* output is actually non-finite so the rule is exercised
352	  directly — not just the budget=NaN case, whose compared outputs are finite. See "Parity fixtures
353	  and non-finite handling" (Implementation Notes).
354	- **Provisional loader diverges from Item 9's protocol.** *Mitigation:* the `PackageLoader`
355	  seam isolates the swap to one module; evidence/evaluator contracts don't change.
356	
357	## Integration Strategy
358	
359	The evaluation layer sits on top of the unchanged executor/validator/router. It **adds** a
360	subpackage and **changes no existing runtime file** (D5 keeps the write-handler workaround local).
361	Item 11 imports `PreparedEvaluator` + `ModelEvidence` + `EvaluationFailed` and drives them exactly
362	as S6's runner drove the probe — the seam is already validated end to end (Item 0, 40/40).
363	Item 9 later swaps `ProvisionalPackageLoader` for its canonical loader and aligns the generated
364	headline vocabulary to `CANONICAL_HEADLINE` (hardening, not blocking).
365	
366	## Validation Approach
367	
368	Kept test suite (all in `packages/teax-simkit/simkit/tests/`, mirroring existing layout):
369	
370	1. **S5's four invariants** — mapping-vs-file case-level parity (INV4); pre-execution rejection
371	   of an invalid typed input before any module runs (INV2); execution-context isolation across
372	   cases (fresh context per `evaluate`, no channel bleed); no output directory in no-persist mode
373	   (INV6).
374	2. **Parity fixture set** — canonical inputs across the three verdict classes; compares selected
375	   outputs (NaN-aware) + verdict statuses (exact), excludes provenance/timestamps/digests/paths/
376	   report-encoding. See "Parity fixtures and non-finite handling" (Implementation Notes) for what
377	   each leg carries and which fixture exercises the NaN-aware rule — **two non-finite fixtures are
378	   mandatory: the budget=NaN indeterminate case and a NaN-propagates-to-a-compared-output case.**
379	3. **Isolation test (two legs, INV1)** — (a) **static AST source scan** of `evidence.py`/
380	   `entry_source.py`/`failure.py`/`projection.py`: parse each module, collect every `import` /
381	   `from … import` node **including those inside `TYPE_CHECKING` and string-annotation blocks**, and
382	   assert every import root is on an **allowlist** (stdlib, `pydantic`, `simkit`-internal) — an
383	   *allowlist*, not a blacklist of generated symbol names, so it is robust to the provisional
384	   package name (`wi014_s4`) and Item 9's rename; (b) **package-absent construction** — import the
385	   four modules and construct a `ModelEvidence` with the generated package absent from `sys.path`,
386	   catching any dynamic `importlib` dependency the static scan can't see. Either leg alone has a
387	   gap; together they have teeth.
388	4. **Three-distinguishable-outcomes test** — a module exception → `module_execution` failure; an
389	   `entry_validation` schema rejection → failure with a different phase; an `indeterminate`
390	   verdict → ordinary evidence, never a failure (SC3, INV5).
391	5. **Non-finite reaches the verdict** — a NaN budget passes entry validation and evaluates to
392	   `indeterminate` (B3).
393	
394	Environment: teax's own working venv is stood up as the **first implementation step** (spec
395	Implementation Prerequisites; the spikes borrowed the fusion-tea venv). Until then, tests run
396	under the licensed host venv per the Item 0 reproduction recipe.
397	
398	## Next-Stage Handoff
399	
400	- **Fixed:** Shape A (D1, owner gate); the four deferred decisions above; the phase→failure map;
401	  the parity equivalence class (from spec); the subpackage layout and isolation-scan boundary (D2).
402	- **Open (plan's to sequence):** venv provisioning first; exact module-by-module port order from
403	  the probe; the fixture files (reuse Item 0's candidate set + the sealed package).
404	- **De-risk first:** the isolation boundary — write INV1's kept test before porting projection,
405	  so the no-generated-import rule is enforced from the first commit rather than retrofitted.
406	
407	---
408	**Next Step:** After approval → `/_my_design_review` (fresh session), then `/_my_plan`.
